analysis.title: ...Flows, Charts & Wrap Up. Nowhere to hide - But now Jensen is BACK. (23 Nov 2026)
key_insights: NVDA +27% pre-market on news the board reinstated Jensen Huang as President and CEO, pulling NDX +6.5% and SPX +4% pre-market, with VIX falling below 28. Author flags choppiness after the first euphoria and cautions that market fate is tied to one person.

NVDA board said it received input from senior US government levels and is confident Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk. Author links this to the SEC probe and speculates about a US-China understanding. Interim CEO Kress had denied a return the prior week.

Prior Friday (20 Nov) was a meltdown: NDX -4.6%, SPX -3.26% intraday with VIX near 28. NDX fell about 11% on the week and is more than 20% off highs, SOX fell 17% on the week, and SPX broke below 7k. Heavy ETF macro selling, expiry and thin top-of-book liquidity added to the move.

Common risk-off driver is a tightening Fed. Williams said inflation is stubbornly high and Waller floated a 50bp hike. Author compares this to 2018, when the Fed hiked into crowded tech as yields broke out.
GS US vol panic index reads 9.8 out of 10. Historically readings above 9.5 have signalled near-term relief. NDX is technically oversold.
Ben Snider's three conditions for an S&P bottom are: improved confidence in AI earnings trajectory, a dovish Fed signal or better macro, and a major drop in investor positioning.
GS FCI has tightened about 100bp this year, all since early September and over 40bp last week alone. Drivers are higher rates, lower equities and a stronger dollar.

Hedge funds net sold US equities for a third straight week, with net selling in 9 of 11 sectors and a +11% spike in ETF shorts. Only Info Tech and Energy were spared. Month-to-date Asia tech/AI saw long sales outpace short additions 2.4-to-1, led by Korea and Taiwan.

CTAs cut global equity length from about $410bn to $290bn vs 3 months ago and sold more than $22bn of S&P last week. They are now short about $10bn, with trend levels at 7650 and 7550 turning negative.

Retail is the incremental buyer, with days of more than $2bn net buying last week, mostly NVDA, AMD, MU and megacaps. Taiwan retail margin balances fell to US$17bn from a US$28bn peak, with aggregate MMR at 132% near the 130% margin-call threshold.

AMD fell 7.7% after a Hunterbrook short report alleging it reached Chinese military-linked entities despite US export controls, raising BIS scrutiny risk. NVDA beat and raised but fell 2.89% T+1 and trades near 9x forward P/E, with GIR at about $18 CY27 EPS.
Apple is the defensive tech play, +26% YTD, and for the first time since the AI boom began is outperforming the NDX. SK Hynix trades near 3x P/E.

GIR is bullish: S&P 500 to 8,700 by end-2027 (+17%), with EPS growth slowing from about 30% in 2026 to 18% in 2027. Hyperscaler cloud growth accelerated from 25% in 2024 to 54% in Q3 2026 with $1.8T backlogs.

Flows: US equity ETF inflows were $59.3bn last week while fixed-income ETF flows fell to $2.6bn after a hot CPI. Global equity funds took in $98bn in the week to Nov 11. Credit strategists expect $2.8T IG and HY issuance in 2027 vs $2.4T in 2026.
Mutual fund positioning: large-cap funds are 722bp underweight Mag 7 and -631bp underweight Info Tech. 81% of large-cap growth funds are outperforming YTD, the highest in over a decade.

Trump, Xi and Putin held a tri-lateral meeting in Shenzhen and issued a joint declaration of peace with no real takeaways, and oil fell. Gold is near $3.5-3.6k, about 37% below peak, and BTC is near $61-62k.

Defensive tech play, +26% YTD, first outperformance of NDX since the AI boom began.

sector_views.rationale: AI trade intact and demand exceeds capacity, but heavy de-grossing and oversold conditions. Another leg lower expected before improvement.
Slight net hedge fund buying as defensives, while funds trimmed tilts.

earnings_insights: NVDA delivered a classic beat and raise last week, but the stock fell 2.89% T+1. Vera Rubin execution was strong and management said the leadership transition has not disrupted customer or supplier relationships.
GIR CY27 NVDA EPS is about $18, a GS estimate, implying about 9x forward P/E.
GS expects S&P 500 EPS growth to slow from roughly 30% in 2026 to 18% in 2027 (forecast).
